cards.text: Big battle shaping up, friend. The Philistines bring all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camps by the spring in Jezreel. Meanwhile David has been living with Achish, king of Gath (1 Samuel 27:2-3).

cards.question: The Philistine leaders march out in units of hundreds and thousands. Who's marching behind them with Achish?

cards.text: The Philistine commanders spot David's crew in the line and ask, “What about these Hebrews?” Friend, that's like strolling into the other team's huddle and asking what the play is.

cards.question: Achish speaks up for David. True or false: he tells the commanders he's found no fault in David from the day he defected until today.

cards.text: The commanders are not convinced. Not a little bit. They're ANGRY with Achish.

cards.question: What do the angry Philistine commanders tell Achish to do with David?

answers.text: Send him back where you assigned him
Put him at the front of the battle
Keep him under guard in the camp

cards.question: The commanders say David must not go down into battle with them, only to become their ___ during the war.

cards.text: Their worry? What better way for David to win back his master's favor than with the heads of their men. Friend, that is ONE way to get your old job back.

cards.question: The commanders back up their worry with a song people sing about David in their dances. What does the song say?

answers.text: Saul has slain his thousands and David his tens of thousands
Saul is our king and David is our mighty shield
David has won the day and Saul has won the war

cards.text: So Achish calls David in and opens with this: “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright.” Achish says he'd be glad to have David march in and out with him in the army.

cards.question: True or false: Achish tells David that the Philistine leaders see him as good too.
So what does Achish tell David to do, so he won't displease the Philistine leaders?

answers.text: Turn back now and go in peace
Stay in camp and guard the supplies
March at the front with the leaders

cards.text: David pushes back: “But what have I done?” I asked that same question the day I got slid into the junk drawer, and nobody answered, because it was a DRAWER.

cards.question: David asks Achish what he's found against him to keep him from going along to fight against the ___ of his lord the king.

cards.text: Achish tells David he's as pleasing in his sight as an angel of God. But the commanders have spoken: he must not go into battle with them.

cards.question: Achish gives David his orders: get up ___ in the morning with the men who came with you, and go as soon as it is ___.
Next morning, David and his men are up early. Where are they headed?

answers.text: Back to the land of the Philistines
Over to Saul's camp at Gilboa

cards.question: True or false: after David leaves, the Philistines go up to Jezreel.

cards.text: The Philistines march one way, and David marches the other. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, but this story's got plenty of road left.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile David has been living with Achish" says David is still living with Achish. 1 Samuel 27:5-7 shows David asked to leave the royal city and settled in Ziklag, the town Achish gave him. The line reads as if he still lives in Gath with the king. It could say David has been serving Achish, or living in Philistine territory under him.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke compares the commanders' question to someone "strolling into the other team's huddle and asking what the play is." The commanders aren't strolling anywhere or asking for the play. They are asking why outsiders are in their own ranks. The comparison gives the commanders' line David's position and a different action, so it doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "The commanders are not convinced. Not a little bit. They're ANGRY with Achish."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Their worry?", the paraphrase of the commanders, and the joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Achish says he'd be glad to have David march in and out with him" states a feeling as fact. 1 Samuel 29:6 says it "seems right in my sight." It should keep the text's wording, or mark the feeling as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new moment in the drawer backstory: Dorin asking "what have I done?" when he was put in the drawer. The backstory never includes this, and invented moments are only allowed around his bakery. The punchline "nobody answered, because it was a DRAWER" also doesn't hold up. Onboarding shows the drawer full of things that talk, so a baker may say "huh?"

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
